name: Skepta
editorial_article:
Chief Joseph Olaitan Adenuga Jr, professionally known as Skepta, is a transformative figure in British music, widely recognized as a primary architect of the global grime sound. Born in 1982 in North London, Adenuga began his musical journey as a DJ within the Tottenham-based Meridian Crew before pivoting to become one of the most formidable MCs in the scene. Alongside his brother Jme and others, he co-founded the influential collective and label Boy Better Know in 2005, a venture that would prove pivotal in maintaining the independent spirit of grime amidst industry pressure.

Skepta's career is marked by a refusal to compromise, most notably seen in his transition from early commercial attempts to the raw, self-produced sound of his 2016 masterpiece, 'Konnichiwa.' That album, featuring seminal tracks such as 'That's Not Me' and 'Shutdown,' earned the Mercury Prize and served as a catalyst for a massive resurgence in grime's global popularity. Beyond his solo work, he has been a bridge between the UK and US hip-hop scenes, with his production and collaborative efforts on tracks like ASAP Rocky’s 'Praise the Lord (Da Shine)' reaching international audiences. A visionary in more than just sound, Skepta's impact extends to fashion, visual arts, and film, securing his place as a central figure in 21st-century British pop culture. He continues to shape the underground and mainstream alike, holding a Nigerian chieftaincy as the 'Amuludun of Odo-Aje,' a testament to his enduring cultural legacy. Skepta's stylistic range spans from early, frantic grime instrumentals to more introspective, bass-heavy explorations in his later work, consistently maintaining an authentic voice that speaks to the realities of London life.
